indication: Symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) in adults and pediatric patients weighing 30 kg or more, to improve functional capacity and symptoms
headline: The FDA approved Camzyos (mavacamten) for pediatric patients weighing 30 kg or more with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on September 30, 2026, the goal date (NDA 214998, supplement 13). Bristol Myers Squibb announced the approval the same day.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for NDA 214998 supplement 13 is dated September 30, 2026 and describes the supplement as extending the indication to pediatric patients weighing 30 kg or more with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, based on the pediatric study CV027010 (SCOUT-HCM) in adolescents aged 12 to 18, with a new 1 mg capsule strength and REMS modifications (FDA approval letter). Bristol Myers Squibb's June 1, 2026 release stated that the FDA had accepted the sNDA for priority review with a PDUFA date of September 30, 2026 (BMS, June 1, 2026); the decision came on that day. Per BMS, SCOUT-HCM (n=44) met its primary endpoint: Valsalva LVOT gradient fell 49.4 mmHg on Camzyos versus 1.8 mmHg on placebo at week 28 (difference 48.0 mmHg, p<0.0001); no patient had LVEF below 50% (BMS release, September 30, 2026). Correction, October 14, 2026: an earlier page on this site dated this approval June 1, 2026; that was the acceptance for review, not the approval.
source_label: FDA approval letter, NDA 214998 supplement 13, September 30, 2026
h1: Camzyos (mavacamten) FDA approval for pediatric obstructive HCM: Sep 30, 2026

drug: neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) - age limit removed, patients 15 kg and over
indication: Emergency treatment of type I allergic reactions including anaphylaxis in adults and pediatric patients weighing 15 kg or more
headline: The FDA approved a labeling change for neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) on March 26, 2026 that removes the age criterion, so the indication now covers adults and pediatric patients weighing 15 kg (33 lb) or more (NDA 214697, supplements 2 and 4). ARS Pharmaceuticals announced it on March 27, 2026.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letters for NDA 214697 supplement 2 (efficacy) and supplement 4 (labeling) are both dated March 26, 2026 (S-002 letter, S-004 letter). ARS announced the approval on March 27, 2026 (ARS release). The 1 mg dose for children weighing 15 to 30 kg was approved separately on March 5, 2025 and has its own page. Correction, October 14, 2026: an earlier page on this site listed a neffy approval announced May 15, 2026; that date was ARS's first-quarter earnings release, which recapped this March approval, not a new FDA action.
source_label: FDA approval letter, NDA 214697 supplement 2, March 26, 2026
h1: neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) FDA approval, age criterion removed: Mar 26, 2026

drug: Optune Pax (Tumor Treating Fields) - locally advanced pancreatic cancer
indication: Adult patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer, concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel
headline: The FDA approved Optune Pax, Novocure's Tumor Treating Fields device for locally advanced pancreatic cancer, on February 11, 2026 (premarket approval P250034). Novocure announced the approval the same day.
pdufa_note: This is a device premarket approval (CDRH), not a drug application. The FDA's PMA database records P250034 with decision date February 11, 2026 for adult patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer, concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (FDA PMA record). Novocure's release of February 11, 2026 is filed as an exhibit to its 8-K (8-K exhibit). Correction, October 14, 2026: an earlier page on this site dated this decision February 12, 2026; the FDA's decision and Novocure's announcement were both February 11.
source_label: Novocure 8-K exhibit, February 11, 2026; FDA PMA P250034 decision February 11, 2026
h1: Optune Pax (Tumor Treating Fields) FDA approval for locally advanced pancreatic cancer: Feb 11, 2026

drug: OTC NARCAN Nasal Spray - 6-count and 24-count multipacks
indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose (over-the-counter naloxone 4 mg nasal spray), new 6-count and 24-count packaging
headline: The FDA approved a packaging supplement for over-the-counter NARCAN Nasal Spray adding 6-count and 24-count multipacks on February 11, 2026 (NDA 208411, supplement 11). Emergent BioSolutions announced it on February 12, 2026.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for NDA 208411 supplement 11 is dated February 11, 2026 (FDA approval letter); Emergent announced the multipacks on February 12, 2026 (Emergent release). This is a packaging and labeling supplement, not a new indication. The separate carrying-case supplement (supplement 10) was approved January 9, 2026 and announced January 14, 2026. Correction, October 14, 2026: an earlier page on this site described a February 13 approval of the carrying case; the February action was the multipack supplement.
source_label: FDA approval letter, NDA 208411 supplement 11, February 11, 2026
h1: OTC NARCAN Nasal Spray FDA approval of 6-count and 24-count multipacks: Feb 11, 2026

drug: Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) - label update, primary CNS lymphoma
indication: a label update removing the limitation of use for primary central nervous system lymphoma (no new indication)
headline: The FDA approved a labeling supplement for Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) on February 5, 2026 that removes the Limitations of Use statement for primary central nervous system lymphoma (BLA 125643, supplement 753). Kite, a Gilead company, announced it on February 6, 2026.
pdufa_note: The FDA's letter for BLA 125643 supplement 753 is dated February 5, 2026 (FDA letter); Gilead announced the label update on February 6, 2026 (Gilead release). This is a labeling change, not a new indication; Yescarta's follicular lymphoma indication (ZUMA-5) is unchanged. Correction, October 14, 2026: an earlier page on this site described this as a ZUMA-5 approval.
h1: Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) FDA label update, primary CNS lymphoma: Feb 5, 2026

indication: Schizophrenia in adults; once-monthly subcutaneous long-acting injectable, 318 mg, 425 mg and 531 mg
headline: The FDA approved Weltruza (olanzapine) for extended-release injectable suspension, Teva's once-monthly subcutaneous long-acting olanzapine for schizophrenia in adults, on October 8, 2026 (NDA 219007). Teva announced the approval on October 9, 2026.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for NDA 219007 is dated October 8, 2026 (FDA approval letter); Drugs@FDA lists the application as received December 8, 2025. Teva announced the approval on October 9, 2026 (Teva release), stating that Weltruza carries no REMS and no post-injection monitoring requirement. pdufa.bio did not hold a goal date for this application, so no early or late margin is computed.
h1: Weltruza (olanzapine) FDA approval for schizophrenia, once-monthly injection: Oct 8, 2026

drug: Tukysa (tucatinib) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab - HER2+ metastatic breast cancer maintenance (HER2CLIMB-05)
indication: Maintenance treatment, in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab, of adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer following induction therapy
headline: The FDA approved Tukysa (tucatinib) in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as maintenance treatment for adults with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer following induction therapy on October 7, 2026 (NDA 213411, supplement 10). Pfizer announced the approval the same day.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for NDA 213411 supplement 10 is dated October 7, 2026 (FDA approval letter); Drugs@FDA lists the supplement as received December 17, 2025. Pfizer's release of October 7, 2026 describes the approval as based on the Phase 3 HER2CLIMB-05 trial (Pfizer release). pdufa.bio did not hold a goal date for this supplement, so no early or late margin is computed.
source_label: FDA approval letter, NDA 213411 supplement 10, October 7, 2026
h1: Tukysa (tucatinib) FDA approval for HER2+ breast cancer maintenance: Oct 7, 2026

drug: Repatha (evolocumab) - cardiovascular risk reduction label expansion (VESALIUS-CV)
indication: To reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unstable angina requiring hospitalization, coronary revascularization, or any ischemia-driven arterial revascularization) in adults at increased risk for these events; label now includes the VESALIUS-CV trial in patients without a prior myocardial infarction or stroke
headline: The FDA approved an efficacy supplement for Repatha (evolocumab) on October 9, 2026 that revises the cardiovascular risk-reduction indication and adds the VESALIUS-CV trial, in adults without a prior heart attack or stroke, to the label (BLA 125522, supplement 47). As of October 14, 2026 Amgen had not issued a release on it.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for BLA 125522 supplement 47 is dated October 9, 2026 and describes labeling modifications based on VESALIUS-CV (trial 20170625) and a revised indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, including any ischemia-driven arterial revascularization, in adults at increased risk for these events (FDA approval letter; revised label). This page is dated by the FDA's action; Amgen's investor site listed no release on this approval as of October 14, 2026. pdufa.bio did not hold a goal date for this supplement, so no early or late margin is computed.
source_label: FDA approval letter, BLA 125522 supplement 47, October 9, 2026
h1: Repatha (evolocumab) FDA approval, VESALIUS-CV label expansion: Oct 9, 2026

drug: OTC NARCAN Nasal Spray - carrying case
indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose (over-the-counter naloxone 4 mg nasal spray), packaged with a carrying case
headline: The FDA approved a supplement for over-the-counter NARCAN Nasal Spray packaged with a carrying case on January 9, 2026 (NDA 208411, supplement 10). Emergent BioSolutions announced it on January 14, 2026.
pdufa_note: The FDA's approval letter for NDA 208411 supplement 10 is dated January 9, 2026 (FDA approval letter); Emergent announced the carrying case on January 14, 2026 (Emergent release). source_label: FDA approval letter, NDA 208411 supplement 10, January 9, 2026
